chain.label: OPC had no structured pilot training program or SOPs
chain.trigger: OPC had no structured pilot training program to ensure that company pilots, including the accident pilot, were proficient in the Beech King Air airplane

chain.label: Pilot's initial and OPC King Air training were both inadequate
chain.trigger: the pilot's initial training did not provide him with adequate experience and proficiency for Beech King Air operations

caused_by.evidence: the Beech King Air 65-A90 flight training that OPC provided to new company pilots was insufficient and did not ensure that the accident pilot... was prepared

chain.label: Airplane not properly repaired/maintained after July 2016 accident
chain.trigger: the accident airplane was not airworthy because it had not been properly repaired after the previous accident

chain.label: Left wing remained twisted, requiring full left-wing-down trim and reducing left-wing stall margin
chain.trigger: the twisted left wing that resulted from the airplane's previous accident reduced the airplane's stall margin

caused_by.evidence: The left wing was not repaired after the July 2016 accident

chain.label: Airplane operated near or beyond aft CG limit due to flawed weight-and-balance formula and unsecured passengers
chain.trigger: the airplane was likely operated near or possibly beyond the aft CG limit during the accident takeoff

chain.label: Pilot performed an intentional aggressive low-altitude high-bank turn with simultaneous pitch-up on takeoff
chain.trigger: the pilot conducted an intentional aggressive takeoff maneuver involving a low-altitude high-bank turn and simultaneous pitch-up maneuver

caused_by.evidence: the pilot's minimal training did not provide him with the necessary experience to fully understand the altered handling qualities of the airplane with a CG that was near the aft limit
the lighter control column forces (due to the airplane's operation near the aft CG limit) could have resulted in an increased airplane pitch response and a subsequently higher AOA

chain.label: Airplane entered an accelerated stall at 100-200 ft altitude
chain.trigger: the pilot likely overcontrolled the airplane during the accident flight... which caused the airplane to enter an accelerated stall

caused_by.evidence: the pilot's aggressive takeoff maneuver caused an accelerated stall
the twisted left wing... likely caused the left wing to stall before the right wing and precipitated the airplane's roll to the left

chain.label: Airplane rolled inverted and entered an unrecoverable loss of control at low altitude
chain.trigger: a subsequent loss of control at an altitude from which recovery was not possible

caused_by.evidence: the airplane's orientation and trajectory at the time of impact were consistent with a sharp turn and loss of control

chain.label: Airplane struck the ground inverted in a 45° nose-down attitude, followed by postcrash fire
chain.trigger: the airplane impacted a grass and dirt area about 630 ft northeast of the departure end of the runway, and a postcrash fire ensued

chain.label: Pilot and all 10 passengers fatally injured; accident not survivable
chain.trigger: The pilot and 10 passengers were fatally injured... The accident was not survivable

caused_by.evidence: The pilot and 10 passengers were fatally injured, and the airplane was destroyed
